transcript:
Meeting header - recorded: 2026-03-18T16:00:00Z | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Zephyr CTO), Jordan Blake (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (DevOps)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I see we have about 40ish minutes. Quick intros, I'm Alex, I'm the AE working with PLG accounts, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya: Hi all, Maya here, CTO at Zephyr. Jordan and Samir are on with me. We're interested in how quickly we can get something into product with Redwood's hosted API and what the lift looks like if we scale to Dedicated or Private later.
[00:25] Priya: Awesome. Quick agenda: 1) PLG quickstart and free credits, 2) integration and time-to-first-token, 3) hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, 4) security/compliance questions, and 5) next steps. Does that work?
[00:36] Jordan: Yep. Mostly want to understand latency & cost, and the path to move to a private deployment later for data residency.

[02:05] Priya: To kick off PLG quickstart: we give free credits for new accounts, there are quickstart templates and SDKs that get you to first token in under 10 minutes for a hello-world. In practice, for a real request roundtrip- our hosted API median TTF (time-to-first-token) is typically 200-400ms for small prompt sizes, though that depends on model choice and sequence length.
[02:30] Samir: 200-400ms, okay is that for the standard curated models or for like larger LLMs? We run longer contexts.
[02:37] Priya: Good callout. That number was for our mid-sized open models (7B-ish). For larger models or longer contexts latency ramps, and we can show you profiling. We also have streaming for chat. For your longer contexts we use KV cache and prefix caching to avoid repeated compute for shared prefixes.
[03:05] Maya: How painful is integration for our team? We have a node/python backend.
[03:10] Alex: The SDKs are official for Python and Node, plus a curl-based REST path. Most customers prototype with the quickstart Node sample, redeem credits, and ship a first feature in a day or two. Time-to-first-token for dev is minutes; production-grade involves some config.

[04:20] Jordan: If we start on hosted, can we later migrate to Dedicated or Private without rework? We have strict data residency needs for some EU customers.
[04:29] Priya: Yes- that's a core Redwood pattern. The API surface and request/response object doesn't change. For Dedicated/Private you pick a deployment mode and you get additional controls: VPC peering, KMS integration, dedicated GPU pools. We do work with you on deployment packaging for private/on-prem but client code typically doesn't change beyond endpoint and auth.
[04:48] Samir: Auth — do you support SAML/SSO for the console and API keys for programmatic? We need RBAC and audit logs.
[04:55] Alex: We support SAML SSO for the console, API keys for services, and RBAC roles. Audit logs and request-level tracing are included for Dedicated/Private; hosted has configurable retention. For customers needing HIPAA/SOC2 we have compliance packages and can discuss SLAs.

[06:10] Priya: Wanted to flag: for Private we provide an optional customer-managed control plane so you retain network isolation. KMS/HSM integrations supported—your keys can encrypt models and KV caches.
[06:22] Maya: Good. How do you handle cost projection? We're concerned about per-token cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[06:30] Priya: We have Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching settings, quantization profiles, and model routing rules. For example you can route low-latency queries to a smaller model and fallback to a higher quality model for expensive requests. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console so you can forecast.
[06:55] Jordan: Can you show an example math for a simple chat use-case?
[07:02] Alex: Sure. If you run 100k messages a month with avg 150 tokens in+out, that's 15M tokens. If model cost is X per 1k tokens, we'll show you the breakdown in the pricing doc I'll send — and apply free credits to offset pilot usage.

[08:40] Maya: For the quickstart, what exactly do we get in the free credits pack? Anything tied to support?
[08:47] Alex: Free credits usually cover enough for a 2-4 week pilot depending on volume; we also include a support path through our PLG onboarding with access to docs and optionally a Solutions Engineer session. For enterprise pilots we do a short-term trial with a bit higher support SLA.

[10:15] Priya: On integration specifics: our Node sample shows installing redwood-sdk, setting REDWOOD_API_KEY, and a 6-line call to create a chat completion. We also have a Postman collection and example infra as IaC for Dedicated.
[10:30] Samir: Any gotchas with proxy or internal egress restrictions? We have an internal firewall that restricts outbound.
[10:38] Priya: For strict egress you can use dedicated private deployments inside your VPC or set up VPC peering. For hosted, we recommend a small NAT rule to allow egress to Redwood endpoints; we can provide IP ranges and FQDNs.

[12:05] Jordan: Performance testing — we'd want to measure 95th percentile latency under production-like load. Do you run benchmarks or provide tooling?
[12:14] Priya: We provide a benchmark template (CSV + load script) and we can help run a baseline with our SEs. For Dedicated we can reserve a GPU pool sized to your throughput and provide guidance on batching parameters to hit your latency SLO. I'll attach the spreadsheet after the call.
[12:40] Maya: If we do a pilot on hosted, would that skew results vs Dedicated hardware?
[12:48] Priya: It can. Hosted is multi-tenant and optimized for general workloads; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and can meet tighter latency SLOs. For an apples-to-apples comparison we recommend a short Dedicated benchmark, but we can often get indicative numbers on hosted first.

[15:20] Alex: Quick pause — any blockers for starting the quickstart?
[15:25] Maya: We need to confirm policies with security and get a budget sign-off, but from engineering side we can try the quickstart.
[15:30] Samir: Also need clarification on data retention and logs for hosted. Are prompt logs stored and for how long?
[15:38] Alex: By default hosted retains request logs for X days (we'll include exact number in docs), and you can enable stricter retention or opt-out with Dedicated/Private where you control retention and logs. We'll send the security pack which includes SOC2, encryption, and retention policies.

[18:00] Jordan: On model choices: what models are in the catalog? We care about smaller models for latency but don't want to lose quality.
[18:08] Priya: We curate open models and provide Redwood-verified profiles. Also provide quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) for cost improvements. Our Optimize tool suggests model + quantization per workload. We can run a quality vs latency eval on your prompts.
[18:40] Maya: For our EU customers, data residency matters. Does Redwood offer regional hosting in EU?
[18:48] Alex: Yes, we have regions in NA and EU, and Private deployments can be configured in customer VPCs in EU cloud regions. We'll note region options in the follow-up.

[21:00] Samir: Regarding security reviews — we have an internal checklist (SAML, audit logs, encryption in flight + at rest, contractual terms). Can you provide standard security artifacts?
[21:10] Alex: Absolutely. We'll share a security deck and a SOC2 summary, an encryption/KMS whitepaper, and SSO setup notes. For particularly sensitive customers we do an architecture review with security folks.

[23:35] Jordan: Any limits on concurrent requests or quotas on the PLG tier?
[23:42] Priya: PLG/self-serve accounts have default rate limits, but they can be increased during a pilot. Dedicated provides reserved capacity for high concurrency. We'll include default rate limits in the docs.

[25:00] Maya: If we want to test routing (e.g., low-cost model for simple tasks, high-quality for critical tasks), is that something we can configure easily?
[25:08] Priya: Yes — you can set per-route model configs and routing policies in the console or via API. You can also configure automatic fallback rules if the preferred model is unavailable.

[27:30] Alex: I'll summarize next steps at the end, but quick commercial question: what's your timeline for a pilot?
[27:36] Maya: We'd like to kick a 2-week pilot asap, ideally next week, pending security sign-off. Target is to get an internal demo to product leadership in about 3 weeks.

[29:10] Priya: Great. For the pilot we'll need: 1) sample prompts/dataset, 2) success metrics (latency targets, quality thresholds), and 3) a point of contact for security. With that we can provision credits and spin up any needed Dedicated sandbox.

[29:35] Maya: We can provide prompts and a small dataset. I'll confirm the security contact.

[31:00] Jordan: Any concerns about vendor lock-in if we switch later?
[31:06] Priya: We design the API to be consistent and use standard formats, and you can pin model versions. Moving between Hosted and Dedicated is an operational change but not a code rewrite; Private has packaging steps but SDK calls remain the same. We also provide exportable logs and request traces for auditing.

[33:10] Samir: For the pilot, will the free credits cover the baseline?
[33:16] Alex: Likely yes for a small pilot. We'll include a sample cost estimate in the follow-up and apply the credits to your account. If you exceed them we'll give notice and discuss options.

[35:00] Maya: Any reference customers in our space? We work in analytics for supply chain.
[35:06] Alex: We have a couple of analytics customers (anonymized) and a case study we can share. I'll include a short references pack.

[36:40] Priya: Technical note — if you care about long sequences we recommend testing KV cache and model quantization; these reduce per-token compute. Also ensure your client handles partial streaming responses if you use streaming chat.

[38:20] Maya: Sounds good. Let's wrap with a recap and next steps.
[38:28] Alex: Recap: 1) Alex will send quickstart guide, free credits redemption, security pack, pricing example and references; 2) Priya will schedule a 1-hour performance deep dive and attach benchmark template; 3) Zephyr (Maya) will share pilot dataset access details and confirm security point of contact.
[38:45] Jordan: Timeline — we aim to start pilot next week; we'll confirm by Friday.
[39:00] Samir: One final question — is there pre-built telemetry for token-level cost in the console?
[39:06] Priya: Yes, token-level cost and per-route breakdowns are in Redwood Console and we'll show screenshots in the follow-up.

[40:30] Maya: Thanks Alex and Priya, this was helpful.
[40:35] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

[41:00] Meeting end.
